coverage.scope: C. Chapter7 Chapter-specific treatment, no routine cramdown, redemption and reaffirmation, full Supreme Court Dewsnup majority and Scalia/Souter dissent interpreting §506(d), lien ride-through and pre-Code practice

topics.title: C. Chapter 7: Undersecured Liens Ride Through Absent Special Relief
topics.description: Why §506(d) cannot simply force a retained-property stripdown and what §722/§524(c) do.

entries.title: Ordinary Chapter7 doesn't offer general forced installment cramdown
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Unlike Chapters11–13 confirmed plans, individual Chapter7 generally has no route forcing lender to accept installment payment of reduced collateral value while debtor keeps asset, without consent.
entries.laymanExplanation: If debtor cannot pay lump sum for car, can't just force bank to accept 5-year plan in Chapter7.
entries.legalExplanation: Instead §722 redemption (qualified personal household property) or §524(c) reaffirmation (consensual) may allow debtor to keep car, subject broader law.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish Chapter7 liquidation from Chapter13 debt adjustment.
entries.examTrap: Chapter7 discharge alone doesn't create automatic right to keep collateral for monthly payments.

entries.title: §722 redemption needs lump sum and personal property conditions
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Chapter7 individual debtor may redeem qualifying exempt or abandoned tangible PERSONAL property intended primarily for personal/family/household use securing dischargeable consumer debt, by paying allowed secured claim amount in one payment.
entries.laymanExplanation: If can borrow cash to buy out lender's lien value, keep household vehicle.
entries.legalExplanation: Price valuation may invoke §506(a)(2) and other conditions under §722.
entries.examApplication: For Chapter6 6.4(a/e) verify both property-use eligibility and appraisal; not just price.
entries.examTrap: Business-only work vehicle typically cannot be redeemed via ordinary §722.

entries.title: §524(c) reaffirmation is consensual and restores personal debt
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Creditor may agree to accept ongoing payments via valid reaffirmation allowing collateral retention; debtor waives discharge protection for reaffirmed debt with procedural safeguards.
entries.laymanExplanation: You can negotiate keep car by agreeing to continue personally owing lender.
entries.legalExplanation: Must satisfy Code's reaffirmation procedures; not a unilateral debtor right.
entries.examApplication: Ask if creditor actually consented or debtor only wrote intention to keep payments current.
entries.examTrap: Do not say reaffirmation automatically occurs by mailing monthly check.

entries.title: Lien can remain enforceable even if borrower is personally discharged
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Long v Bullard traditional rule: in rem lien rides through bankruptcy, even though personal judgment claim discharged; secured creditors enforce against pledged property within law.
entries.laymanExplanation: Personal debt collection may end, but bank can still foreclose property after case if lien remains.
entries.legalExplanation: §506(d) does not generally authorize Chapter7 valuation-based elimination of otherwise valid allowed lien per Dewsnup.
entries.examApplication: Explain collateral recovery versus deficiency suit against discharged person.
entries.examTrap: Don't confuse §727 discharge of personal debt with lien avoidance.

topics.title: C. Dewsnup v. Timm (1992) — Full Opinion and Scalia Dissent
topics.description: No Chapter7 §506(d) lien stripdown; statutory phrase 'allowed secured claim' versus §506(a).

entries.title: Dewsnup v. Timm, 502 U.S. 410 (1992)
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: No. Supreme Court affirmed: §506(d) does not authorize reduction of lien where creditor's underlying claim is ALLOWED under §502 and SECURED BY a valid lien, even if §506(a) valuation leaves deficiency unsecured for distribution. Pre-Code principle preserves liens through Chapter7 until foreclosure/payment.
entries.laymanExplanation: In ordinary Chapter7, §506(d) does not permit stripdown of otherwise valid lien securing allowed claim merely because collateral's present value is below debt; lien survives even while §506(a) splits claim for bankruptcy distribution.
entries.legalExplanation: Blackmun majority said §506 text had ambiguity and interpreted 'allowed secured claim' in §506(d) as claim allowed plus backed by security rather than full §506(a) value-defined term. Deference to longstanding pre-Code lien survival, absent clear congressional indication of new lien-stripping remedy. Reducing lien would let debtor take windfall of later collateral appreciation that lender originally bargained for; creditor who participates in case shouldn't forfeit property rights. Cited Long v Bullard and Radford. Scalia/Souter dissent argued same phrase 'allowed secured claim' must mean same thing in adjacent §506(a)/(d), plain text voids unsecured lien part and majority used pre-Code practice to override statutory words.
entries.examApplication: Compute debt ~120k, appraised land $39k, then discuss why no reduction of actual lien despite §506(a) classification. Compare Chapter13 plan cramdown.
entries.examTrap: Dewsnup is chapter-context-sensitive; it doesn't eliminate separately authorized reorganization bifurcation/cramdown, avoidances, or redemption.
entries.sourceRole: Full Supreme Court opinion and Scalia dissent excerpted in Chapter 6
entries.facts: Aletha and T. LaMar Dewsnup granted deed of trust on two Utah farm parcels for $119,000 loan in June1978; loan defaulted and foreclosure threatened, debtor filed Chapter7 June1984. In 1987 debtor filed adversary seeking §506 lien reduction, alleging debt about $120k while collateral worth $39k; lower courts rejected despite appraised value. Debtor argued §506(a) secured portion limited to property value and §506(d) voided remaining lien.
entries.issue: Can Chapter7 debtor invoke §506(a) secured-value definition combined with §506(d) lien voiding to strip lien down from fully allowed debt to current lower collateral market value?
entries.holding: No. Supreme Court affirmed: §506(d) does not authorize reduction of lien where creditor's underlying claim is ALLOWED under §502 and SECURED BY a valid lien, even if §506(a) valuation leaves deficiency unsecured for distribution. Pre-Code principle preserves liens through Chapter7 until foreclosure/payment.
entries.reasoning: Blackmun majority said §506 text had ambiguity and interpreted 'allowed secured claim' in §506(d) as claim allowed plus backed by security rather than full §506(a) value-defined term. Deference to longstanding pre-Code lien survival, absent clear congressional indication of new lien-stripping remedy. Reducing lien would let debtor take windfall of later collateral appreciation that lender originally bargained for; creditor who participates in case shouldn't forfeit property rights. Cited Long v Bullard and Radford. Scalia/Souter dissent argued same phrase 'allowed secured claim' must mean same thing in adjacent §506(a)/(d), plain text voids unsecured lien part and majority used pre-Code practice to override statutory words.
entries.rule: In ordinary Chapter7, §506(d) does not permit stripdown of otherwise valid lien securing allowed claim merely because collateral's present value is below debt; lien survives even while §506(a) splits claim for bankruptcy distribution.
entries.dissent: Justice Scalia (joined by Justice Souter): phrase 'allowed secured claim' has identical meaning in §506(a) and §506(d). Since §506(a) says only $39k is secured, §506(d) by plain text voids lien above that. Court's pre-Code/custom and purported ambiguity are policy substitutes for statutory text; concern that 'one subsection at a time' interpretation undermines predictable reading.

entries.title: Majority's allowed + secured reading versus §506(a) classification
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: §506(d)'s 'allowed secured claim' understood as claim ALLOWED under §502 and secured by actual lien, not necessarily limited to §506(a)'s collateral-value portion.
entries.laymanExplanation: Court says valid mortgage survives on land even if land presently appraised far below debt.
entries.legalExplanation: Avoids automatic lien voiding and matches pre-Code liens-pass-through tradition; controversial inconsistency with adjacent phrase.
entries.examApplication: If professor asks textual meaning explain both interpretations instead of a conclusory statement.
entries.examTrap: Don't say §506(a) itself disappears from Chapter7 distribution.

entries.title: Pre-Code lien ride-through and appreciation rationale
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Court emphasized secured creditor bargained for lien remaining attached until foreclosure, including opportunity to benefit from postvaluation land appreciation. Stripping would divert upside to debtor.
entries.laymanExplanation: Land could rise from $39k to $100k before foreclosure; lienholder did not agree to lose that appreciation.
entries.legalExplanation: Supreme Court used Long v Bullard and historical practice, and found absence of clear congressional departure in text/legislative history.
entries.examApplication: Use appreciation as policy argument and disclose Scalia textual rebuttal.
entries.examTrap: This does not mean secured lender can collect unlimited more than debt owed.

entries.title: Scalia dissent: identical statutory terms mean same thing
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Scalia contended 'allowed secured claim' appears explicitly defined by §506(a), and §506(d) voids lien 'to extent' secured claim not allowed; majority's contrary rule manufactures ambiguity and defers to history.
entries.laymanExplanation: A definition shouldn't change from one neighboring subsection to another.
entries.legalExplanation: He criticized inconsistency with Ron Pair text-first style; majority used historical principles rather than same-language presumption.
entries.examApplication: On essay compare textualism vs preservation of pre-Code practice.

entries.title: Does Dewsnup bar plan cramdown in Chapter11–13? No
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Dewsnup held Chapter7 debtor cannot use §506(d) as standalone lien-reduction tool; Chapter11–13 statutory plan cramdowns arise from §1129/1225/1325 and may reduce payment/lien rights subject exceptions.
entries.laymanExplanation: Chapter7 and Chapter13 have different legal machinery.
entries.legalExplanation: Casebook explicitly asks whether holding extends to reorganization; Code has express plan modifications that Dewsnup didn't erase.
entries.examApplication: Cite specific plan confirmation section rather than assuming §506(d) alone.
entries.examTrap: Don't extrapolate no-Chapter7-stripdown into universal anti-stripdown.

entries.title: Redemption not surplusage on Scalia reading (his response)
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Scalia argued §722 still necessary even if §506(d) reduced lien, because §722 supplies affirmative right to redeem property by payment, not merely measure lien.
entries.laymanExplanation: Reducing recorded debt on lien isn't same as forcing creditor to transfer/release property after redemption cash.
entries.legalExplanation: Court raised compatibility concern between §506(d) and §722; dissent answered separate functions.
entries.examApplication: Discuss if asked 'why would someone redeem if already stripped lien'.
entries.examTrap: Again this is dissent, not holding.

entries.title: Interpretation methodology: textual coherence vs historical practice
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: Majority found enough ambiguity to consult pre-Code expectations and policy; dissent thought statutory phrase unambiguous and same-meaning canon controlled.
entries.laymanExplanation: Which matters more: clear Code terms or mortgage bargains under prior bankruptcy law?
entries.legalExplanation: Book probes creditor vs debtor fairness and statute reading, including Scalia sarcasm about 'natural justice'.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish legal holding from questions inviting normative critique.
entries.examTrap: No need assert one methodology universally governs all Code sections.

entries.title: Chapter7 secured lender retains in rem rights even after discharge
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights casebook, Chapter 6 §C (Chapter7 stripdown and full Dewsnup v. Timm majority/Scalia dissent), source-based only
entries.summary: The bar on §506(d) ordinary stripping permits mortgage lien to persist; §524(a) discharge protects personal debtor but not pledged land unless lien avoided or paid.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank can foreclose property, not collect unpaid discharged shortfall personally.
entries.legalExplanation: Secured claim may be undersecured for estate payout, but lien still valid after case.
entries.examApplication: Write separate columns allowed secured claim §506(a), surviving in rem lien, discharged personal liability.
entries.examTrap: Avoid saying entire debt was fully secured for §726 payouts.
